pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() adds the label for non-normal items. The 'AC-2' test checks the exact list entries.
The WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id query is covered by the 'AC-3' test, which checks the items and their order for high, low and normal.
The 'AC-4' test checks the unfiltered list and its order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter as <strong>.
The 'AC-6' test checks High, urgent, empty and __proto__ values for a 400 and no <li>. The code uses a Set, so __proto__ is safe.

The 'AC-7' test checks the exact messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in every view with an empty table. The later weakening of the separate state test does not remove this coverage.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test checks it, and traffic/src/index.js appends the path, query included, to the request URL.

findings.what:
Commit fbf13a9 ('Follow-up edits') loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns null when there is no

, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The spec's 'No match' state row now has no state-level check of its message. Only the AC-7 test still checks the exact text. The spec records no justification for the change.
The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened an assertion in test/priority.test.js.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion so the claim is true, or disclose the loosening and the reason.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the spec, apart from the traffic-config check relaxation the change needs to carry a query route.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and each is named by a test. Every state row has a test, but the 'No match' state test was weakened in the last commit.

I did not run the tests, because they need the Workers vitest runtime and CI runs them. By reading, the tests assert real behaviour. The one exception is the 'No match' assertion loosened to toBeDefined(). The fake-app change in test/traffic.test.js is additive.
The README describes the filter. The spec is consistent with the code.
The 400 validation, the parameterised SQL and the empty-message logic are correct. No defects found.

The query is parameterised and the value is checked against an allowlist. Titles are HTML-escaped. The priority value in the nav and the empty message comes only from the allowlist. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the plain server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and the repo has no UI or style assets.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate. The server-rendered output is covered by the fetch-based tests.
The PR's claim that no tests were loosened is false, because of the final commit.
